<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">A benchmark for evaluating atomic visual world knowledge in Multimodal LLMs.</strong></p>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Authors</strong> Kimi Team</p>
<hr class="mt-[7px] mb-4 border-t-[0.5px] border-(--Separators-S1)"/>
<h2 node="[object Object]">Overview</h2>
<p><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-02-13/1d67h1af6rtp4tqfle8mg?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="main figure" srcSet="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-02-13/1d67h1af6rtp4tqfle8mg?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_480 480w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-02-13/1d67h1af6rtp4tqfle8mg?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_800 800w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-02-13/1d67h1af6rtp4tqfle8mg?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1200 1200w, https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-02-13/1d67h1af6rtp4tqfle8mg?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1%2Fformat%2Cwebp%2Fresize%2Cw_1600 1600w" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<p>We are releasing <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">WorldVQA</strong>, a new benchmark designed to measure the factual correctness of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). While recent models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in visual reasoning and description, measuring their reliability regarding visual world knowledge remains a challenge.</p>
<p>WorldVQA focuses on a critical question: <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Does the model actually recognize the specific entity it sees, or is it merely hallucinating based on visual patterns?</strong></p>
<p>Our results show that WorldVQA creates a significant challenge for frontier models. Even state-of-the-art models struggle to achieve high accuracy on long-tail visual knowledge, often falling below 50% accuracy. This benchmark aims to drive progress toward more factually reliable and knowledgeable multimodal AI.</p>
<h2 node="[object Object]">The Dataset</h2>
<p>The dataset consists of <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">3,500</strong> high-quality image-question pairs. The distribution aims to test a model&#x27;s encyclopedic breadth across the world. The dataset distinguishes itself through three core design principles:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Factuality &amp; Unambiguity:</strong> Every question has a single, verifiable ground-truth answer. We exclude subjective questions or ambiguous visual scenarios.</li>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Rich Taxonomy:</strong> The dataset spans 9 categories to ensure broad coverage of world knowledge.</li>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Head vs. Tail Distribution:</strong> We explicitly separate data into <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Head</strong> (common knowledge) and <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Tail</strong> (rare/long-tail knowledge). This allows us to measure how model performance degrades as knowledge becomes more obscure.</li>
</ul>
<blockquote class="border-l-4 border-(--Colors-KMBlue) bg-(--Fills-F1) px-5 py-4 rounded-r-lg rounded-l-none my-6 [&amp;_p]:m-0 [&amp;_p]:text-(--Labels-Primary)">
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Note on Quality</strong>: To ensure the benchmark is a reliable gold standard, all images and question-answer pairs underwent rigorous multi-stage human verification to filter out noise and ambiguity.</p>
</blockquote>

<h2 node="[object Object]">Using WorldVQA to compare models</h2>
<!--$?--><template id="B:0"></template><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:360px"></div></div>
<hr class="mt-[7px] mb-4 border-t-[0.5px] border-(--Separators-S1)"/>
<h2 node="[object Object]">Measuring Calibration: Confidence vs. Accuracy</h2>
<p>In our experiments comparing model confidence with actual accuracy, we utilized two key metrics to measure the alignment between a model&#x27;s subjective belief and its objective performance:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">ECE (Expected Calibration Error):</strong> Measures the average gap between the model&#x27;s subjective confidence and its objective accuracy. The ideal value is <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">0</strong>.</li>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Slope (Weighted Average Slope):</strong> Measures the correlation and sensitivity between the model&#x27;s accuracy and its own confidence. The ideal value is <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">1.0</strong>.</li>
</ul>
<div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGridContainer"><div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGrid" style="gap:16px"><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-02-03/1d60v7i2av1fc64559d50?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="Reliability diagram showing model calibration - Actual Accuracy vs Stated Confidence" loading="lazy" class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__gridImage" style="flex:1;max-width:50%"/><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-02-03/1d60v81aav1fc64559ekg?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="Confidence score distribution across models on WorldVQA benchmark" loading="lazy" class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__gridImage" style="flex:1;max-width:50%"/></div><p class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageCaption"><strong>Calibration and Confidence Distribution Analysis. Left:</strong> Reliability diagrams plotting Actual Accuracy against Stated Confidence. To ensure statistical significance, only bins containing more than 20 samples are visualized. The size of each data point is proportional to the number of samples in that bin. The black dashed diagonal (y=x) represents perfect calibration, while colored dashed lines indicate the weighted average slope for each model. <strong>Right:</strong> The distribution of stated confidence scores across the full dataset (without sample thresholding). The plots reveal a severe overconfidence trend, with most models concentrating their predictions in the 90-100% confidence range.</p></div>
<p>Our experiments reveal that all evaluated models are currently far from the ideal state, exhibiting a universal tendency toward overconfidence.</p>
<p>While <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Kimi-K2.5</strong> achieves best performance on both metrics—recording an ECE of <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">37.9%</strong> and a Slope of <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">0.550</strong>—there remains a significant gap to bridge in the pursuit of &quot;honesty&quot; and &quot;alignment.&quot; Enhancing the self-awareness boundaries of multimodal models represents a critical direction for future exploration.</p>
<h2 node="[object Object]">Conclusion</h2>
<p>WorldVQA is a simple but challenging benchmark for evaluating the atomic visual knowledge of frontier models. Improving performance on WorldVQA is a necessary step for the next generation of AI agents. We are open-sourcing the WorldVQA dataset and evaluation scripts to help the community address the visual knowledge gap.</p>
